title: A Letter for the Ledger Revisited
premise: Isandro Kavanagh, a night-shift dispatcher for Halcyon Cabs, finds the diary of missing accountant Vera Ostrander in a returned taxi — but its entries continue three weeks past her disappearance, written in her hand, describing things only Isandro could know. As he follows the diary's coded references to a ledger hidden in the taxi company's own fare records, he discovers Vera faked her death to expose an embezzlement scheme run by the company's beloved founder, and that someone inside the dispatch office is feeding the killer information. At the anniversary dinner held in Vera's honor, Isandro decodes the final ledger entry, confronts the murderer — his mentor, dispatch chief Odile Voss — and helps Vera step out of hiding to testify, choosing truth over the loyalty that nearly destroyed them both.
about_author: Beatrix Yarrow is the pen name of a former municipal records clerk who spent eleven years cataloguing other people's paper trails before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary workers who notice what institutions prefer to forget.

chapters.title: The Cab That Came Back Empty
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Isandro's POV. A cab returns to the Halcyon lot at 3 a.m. with no driver and a woman's diary wedged under the seat. Isandro recognizes the name inside: Vera Ostrander, missing for six weeks, presumed dead. The beat is quiet unease — the first wrong note in an ordinary night.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reading the diary in the break room, he finds dated entries continuing weeks beyond Vera's disappearance, including one that describes him reading it. He tells no one, torn between reporting the book and protecting himself. Emotional beat: creeping self-doubt as evidence points inward.

chapters.title: Odile's Rules of the Night
chapters.summary: Introduces dispatch chief Odile Voss through Isandro's admiring eyes: she taught him everything, keeps the night shift running like clockwork, and asks pointed questions about the returned cab. Beat: warmth laced with the reader's first hint of surveillance.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: The company announces a memorial dinner for Vera on the anniversary of her disappearance; the founder, Ambrose Halcyon, will attend. Isandro realizes the diary's final entry names that date. Beat: a ticking clock installed beneath civic grief.

chapters.title: Fares That Don't Add Up
chapters.summary: Isandro cross-checks the diary against dispatch logs and finds trips billed to addresses that don't exist. Whose POV alternates here with a brief italicized diary excerpt from Vera. Beat: the thrill of pattern recognition curdling into fear.

chapters.title: A Man Who Rides Nowhere
chapters.summary: Following one phantom address, Isandro interviews a retired driver who once ferried 'packages' for Ambrose after midnight. The driver is nervous, then silent, then gone by morning. Beat: the cost of asking questions made literal.

chapters.title: What the Diary Knows About Me
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, intimate and paranoid. A new diary entry appears in his locker, describing a conversation he had alone. Either Vera is alive and watching, or someone wants him to believe she is. Beat: isolation deepens; he stops trusting his own senses.

chapters.title: Odile's Ledger Hand
chapters.summary: Isandro notices the diary's coded numbers match a shorthand Odile uses on shift sheets. He tests her with a false detail and watches it travel to Ambrose's office within hours. Beat: heartbreak — the mentor is the leak.

chapters.title: Vera's Sister
chapters.summary: Isandro tracks down Vera's estranged sister, Nell, who received one postcard after the disappearance: a taxi medallion number. Together they decode it as a pickup point. Beat: alliance formed; grief shared becomes purpose.

chapters.title: The Midnight Fare
chapters.summary: Nell and Isandro stake out the pickup point and glimpse a living woman matching Vera's description entering a storage unit. They choose not to approach, fearing they're followed. Beat: hope arrives hand-in-hand with danger.

chapters.title: Ambrose's Toast
chapters.summary: At a pre-dinner press event, Ambrose Halcyon performs grief beautifully while announcing a scholarship in Vera's name. Isandro watches the crowd love him and understands how the scheme survived so long. Beat: power's charisma rendered seductive and sickening.

chapters.title: Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Isandro realizes the embezzled amounts are encoded in years of fare records — every tenth trip, rounded up, skimmed to shell companies. The diary's numbers are the key. Beat: revelation; the whole city's routine was the crime scene.

chapters.title: Someone Follows Nell
chapters.summary: Nell is tailed home; her apartment is searched but nothing taken — a message, not a theft. Isandro realizes they're being managed, not stopped, which means the killer needs something from them. Beat: dread reframed as leverage.

chapters.title: The Night Odile Breaks
chapters.summary: Confronted privately, Odile confesses partially: she moved money years ago to pay her mother's debts and has been Ambrose's instrument since. She warns Isandro off before the dinner. Beat: loyalty vs. truth embodied; pity without absolution.

chapters.title: Diary Entry: The Last Ride
chapters.summary: A full chapter in Vera's voice via the diary: how she discovered the ledger, staged her death with help from one insider (unnamed), and kept writing to leave a trail only a dispatcher could read. Beat: the victim becomes the author of the plot.

chapters.title: Counting Down the Glasses
chapters.summary: Two days before the dinner. Isandro copies the decoded ledger onto microfilm-style proof, hides duplicates, and maps exits from the banquet hall. Odile watches him do it and says nothing. Beat: preparation as suspense; every ally now suspect.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The dinner begins: toasts, slideshows, Ambrose's eulogy. Isandro slips away during the third toast to retrieve the original ledger page from the company safe. Beat: elegance stretched over panic.

chapters.title: Caught in the Safe Room
chapters.summary: Ambrose catches Isandro at the safe; Odile arrives — and turns her radio call sign over to Ambrose, revealing she was his enforcer all along, not merely compromised. Isandro is locked in as the toast concludes upstairs. Beat: betrayal at its deepest cut.

chapters.title: Vera Walks In
chapters.summary: Vera Ostrander enters the dinner alive, having coordinated with Nell when Isandro missed his check-in. Chaos erupts; Ambrose's composure cracks publicly. Beat: catharsis — the dead woman raises the glass herself.

chapters.title: The Last Dispatch
chapters.summary: Climax. Ambrose attempts to flee through the garage using a phantom-fare escape route from his own ledger; Odile, realizing he'll make her the fall target, radios his position to police instead. Isandro talks Ambrose's driver down over dispatch like a fare gone wrong. Beat: Isandro's ordinary skill becomes the decisive weapon.

chapters.title: Testimony in Daylight
chapters.summary: Aftermath: arrests, the ledger entered as evidence, Odile charged alongside Ambrose though her cooperation earns leniency. Vera explains why she chose Isandro — a stranger who reads patterns honestly. Beat: justice administered without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Night Shift, Again
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Isandro returns to dispatch under new management. The last diary page, left for him, thanks him and closes the account. He answers a routine late-night call, changed but steady. Beat: quiet resolution — the night continues, and now he keeps its true records.
